rounds.fact: Winamp's slogan 'It really whips the llama's ass' became one of the most recognizable taglines of the early MP3 era, and its skinnable interface inspired an entire community of custom designs.
Answers.com built its early traffic by aggregating dictionary, encyclopedia, and reference content into a single searchable site, well before crowdsourced Q&A sites took over that space.
Netscape's browser dominated the early web so completely that Microsoft bundling Internet Explorer with Windows to compete became the center of a landmark antitrust case.
Twitter launched in 2006 and the 140-character limit came directly from SMS constraints, since early tweets were literally sent and received as text messages.
Yahoo started as a hand-curated web directory. By 1998 its homepage was one of the busiest link farms on the internet, a portal trying to be everyone's front door to the web.
